definition: A tall, branching weed of the daisy family (Lapsana communis) with small yellow flower-heads, found along hedgerows, walls, and disturbed ground; once used in folk medicine and as a pot-herb.
etymology: From nipple, itself tracing to Old English neap or a Low German cognate meaning a small protuberance, plus wort, the Old English wyrt meaning plant or root — a word-forming element that names hundreds of old English herbs. The plant earned its curious name from the supposed resemblance of its closed buds to a nipple, and from the doctrine of signatures, which held that such a resemblance signaled medicinal virtue for the part it echoed. Gerard catalogued it in his 1597 Herball still half-skeptical of the claim.
usage: By late October the nipplewort had gone entirely to seed, its wiry stems rattling against the churchyard wall, unremarked by anyone who had not once been taught to notice it.
